concepts.title: Geography as an Integrating Discipline and Its Branches
concepts.definition: Geography integrates the study of physical and human environments over the earth's surface, synthesising spatial and temporal relations, and divides into physical geography of geomorphology, climatology, hydrology and biogeography, and human geography of social, economic, population and settlement geography with branches of regional studies and spatial analysis.
concepts.key_idea: The word geography comes from Greek meaning earth description, and its dual approach studies both the natural and the cultural landscape.

concepts.title: Physical Geography and Its Importance
concepts.definition: Physical geography deals with earth's surface processes of landforms, weather and climate, water, soils, plants and animals as integrated systems, explaining the spatial distribution of natural phenomena and their influence on human life.
concepts.key_idea: Understanding geomorphic, climatic and biotic processes helps in resource use, hazard preparedness and environmental management.

concepts.title: Latitude, Longitude and the Study of the Earth's Surface
concepts.definition: Geography uses coordinates of latitude and longitude, maps, scales and remote sensing to locate and explain phenomena on the earth's surface, making it the study of areal differentiation and spatial organisation of both physical and human features.
concepts.key_idea: Locating places precisely through the grid of parallels and meridians is the first step of all geographical analysis.
